extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers; clinical trial investigators and study staff implementing hair-based pharmacokinetic/adherence measures
extracted.subtask_short: R01 research strategy for hair-based PK
extracted.subtask_description: Research grant proposal research strategy describing aims, study populations, data collection, laboratory assays, statistical methods, human subjects protections, and monitoring/quality assurance for using hair concentrations to measure adherence and pharmacokinetics in PrEP/treatment trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling undetectable assay values
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat undetectable levels as equal to the detection limit. Add the detection limit to all values before transformation to reduce the influence of small differences between very low hair levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids over-emphasizing tiny differences near zero when transforming (e.g., log) and standardizes treatment of below-LOQ results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of concordance/discordance between hair and plasma levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Concordance and discordance between hair and plasma concentrations of TFV/FTC (or other drugs) provide information on patterns of adherence: high plasma but low/undetectable hair suggests dosing only shortly before visits; detectable hair despite undetectable plasma could indicate ongoing intermittent use with episodic higher use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinations of matrices (hair, plasma, residual ring) to infer timing and patterns of use rather than relying on a single specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study population eligibility for Aim 2 (MTN-025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include HIV-negative women enrolled in MTN-025, composed of former participants of the placebo-controlled phase 3 MTN-020 trial (ASPIRE) who remained HIV-noninfected, are not pregnant, and wish to enroll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated enrollment ~70–85% of ASPIRE women (~1800 participants) from Malawi, South Africa, Uganda and Zimbabwe; use these inclusion rules to define the analytic cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection schedule for dapivirine ring (Aim 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants receive a 25mg dapivirine vaginal ring replaced monthly over 12 months; collect hair, plasma and used rings at each visit (monthly first 3 months, then quarterly) where a ring was used and at the exit visit (one month after product end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a survey on self-reported adherence asking about days the ring was out over the past month and overall use rating; collect specimens according to the specified visit schedule for consistent longitudinal measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory assay validation and LOQ requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use validated assays for plasma and hair (e.g., ultra-performance LC-MS/MS-based assay with a lower limit of quantification of 20 pg/mL for dapivirine in plasma); established extraction and HPLC methods for used rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure laboratory methods are previously developed/validated for small hair samples and specify central laboratories for plasma (e.g., Johns Hopkins) to maintain assay consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy for case-control analysis of seroconverters
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect hair samples from all visits in all seroconverters and from visits of randomly sampled controls at a 3:1 control:case ratio; with ~1800 participants x 7 visits estimate 12,600 hair samples available and analyze ~7 visits from 60 cases and 180 controls (240 x 7 = 1680 samples) for the case-control analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve unassayed samples for other studies; use the same sampling strategy as Aim 1 methods to ensure comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical modeling approach for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pooled logistic regression to estimate the association of dapivirine levels in hair with HIV seroconversion, controlling for covariates associated with HIV risk collected in the trial (age, region, marital status, attitudes toward ring efficacy, alcohol/drug use, anxiety/depression, sexual activity, condom use, vaginal practices, presence of STD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare explanatory utility of self-reported adherence, plasma concentrations, and residual ring levels against hair levels; consider using combinations of two, three, or all four measures and use fitted model parameters to estimate hair levels associated with high protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and sample size thresholds for Aim 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate ~60 seroconversions; analyze 60 cases and 180 controls (3:1). Calculations indicate ≥80% power if the relative risk in the lowest quartile of hair levels versus the top three quartiles is ≥2.9 (seroconversion rate 6.6% in lowest quartile vs 2.3% in others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple observations per person (n=7) improve power and precision; use the framework described in Aim 1 for sample size calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation analyses between matrices and self-report
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine scatterplots and Spearman correlation coefficients between hair, plasma and residual ring concentrations of dapivirine, and with self-reported adherence measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these correlations to quantify concordance across measures and to inform which measures best explain seroconversion outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictors of adherence — modeling approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform univariate linear mixed effects regression models using hair levels as a continuous outcome, include covariates (including residual ring levels and candidate predictors collected in MTN-025), then build multivariate models by forward stepwise selection to assess independent associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also examine how associations of plasma, residual ring, and self-report with hair levels change when controlling for other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 3 study population and inclusion (A5359)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study population composed of individuals on long-acting cabotegravir (LA CAB) in ACTG A5359 — treatment-experienced, diverse HIV-infected individuals with prior non-adherence; only participants randomized to the long-acting arm will be included in hair analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document trial design steps (oral induction, randomization to injectables) and eligibility tied to the parent ACTG trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection schedule for LA cabotegravir (Aim 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: After oral lead-in, participants receive intramuscular injections of LA CAB and rilpivirine every 4 weeks up to 76 weeks; measure HIV RNA every 4–8 weeks and collect hair/plasma samples quarterly for PK monitoring; note and document missed or delayed visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this population is non-adherent, schedule flexibility and documentation of missed visits is critical for correct PK interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation and prediction of trough plasma levels using hair
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess correlations between hair and plasma levels every 12 weeks and use mixed effects linear models for repeated measures (7 measurements per participant) to assess how well hair levels predict trough plasma levels, evaluating CAB levels in each hair segment and averages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage repeated measures and segmental hair data to improve predictive models for trough concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covariates to model factors associated with CAB exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine sex, race/ethnicity, BMI, age, renal and hepatic function, drug and alcohol use, and other factors in relation to hair and plasma concentrations at the end of the dosing interval to assess differential exposure patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model trough levels both as continuous outcomes and categorized per potential protective thresholds; explore which covariates explain variability in exposure and decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefined protective efficacy thresholds (4x PA-IC90)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protective efficacy for LA CAB is modeled to be achieved if plasma levels exceed 4x the protein-adjusted 90% inhibitory concentration (PA-IC90) — estimated 4x PA-IC90 in plasma = 0.66 µg/mL, corresponding to an estimated hair concentration of 66 ng/mg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine factors associated with trough levels relative to these thresholds and analyze levels both continuously and dichotomized around such a priori cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segmental hair analysis protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Use segmental analysis by cutting hair into 0.25 cm sections; each segment reflects average systemic CAB concentration over its growth period (~1 cm per 4 weeks, so 0.25 cm ≈ 1 week).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use segments to map week-by-week exposure (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th weeks post-injection); in cases of missed visits segmental analysis of longer lengths (2–3 cm) can reveal PK impact of lapses; examine decay by comparing last 2–3 segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size considerations for Aim 3 (precision of correlations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample size limited to LA CAB arm (N at least 150); an observed correlation of 0.8 among N=150 at one time point would have a 95% CI from 0.73 to 0.85, and repeated-measures models will use all data for improved assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize exploratory nature due to novelty of injectables but justify cost-efficiency of hair sampling and expected precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory analysis approach for virologic suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multivariate random effects logistic regression models for repeated measures to estimate association of CAB hair and plasma levels (alone and combined) with virologic suppression (<50 copies/mL); evaluate segment-specific and average levels, model thresholds vs continuous/multi-category forms, and use thresholds as outcomes if they perform well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare classification/performance of dichotomized thresholds against continuous modeling; if thresholds validated, use them for outcome modeling of factors associated with achieving protective levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects risk assessment for hair collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Hair collection (approximately 50–100 strands) takes ~90 seconds and is usually painless; small risk of scalp cut exists but no injuries reported in past studies; collection generally acceptable (>95%) when incorporated with education and consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address concerns about hair style disruption and male-pattern baldness; do not collect from completely bald scalps and avoid pubic/axillary hair to minimize variability; include information in IRB-approved consent forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and trial registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed hair collection into trials already registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (SEARCH NCT01864603, MTN-025 NCT02858037; A5359 to be registered) and operate within existing DSMB and IRB/EC approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH/ACTG guidelines for data systems and ensure registration and approvals are in place prior to sample collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data safety and monitoring plan (frequency and responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data monitoring and quality assurance performed ongoingly; project coordinators and statisticians will monitor study data monthly for consent forms, questionnaires, and hair collection rates; DSMBs review adverse events, enrollment, and protocol deviations; all project staff report adverse events to site project managers who escalate to protocol chairs/co-chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear reporting chains and monthly oversight to ensure participant safety and data integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance processes for hair collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Train field staff (presentations at meetings), provide pictures and videos showing collection from varied hair styles, use real-time screening (pictures or shipped samples) to ensure proper collection and labeling, utilize Frontier Sciences LDMS for NIH CTU trials, and re-train sites failing to collect adequate quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement processes to reduce pre-analytic variation and ensure consistent sample quality across multi-site studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities reporting and targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and plan for inclusion: SEARCH PrEP Aim 1 includes ~6400 participants from East Africa (~50% women); MTN-025 Aim 2 composed entirely of women; A5359 Aim 3 expected diverse race/ethnicity (~30% African American, up to 20% Latino, ~25% women).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PHS inclusion enrollment reporting formats (but not for collecting participant data) to document planned and cumulative enrollment by sex/gender and race/ethnicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of children (age-based consent rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEARCH PrEP allows enrollment ≥15 years (15–17 require parental co-consent); MTN-025 only enrolled women 18–45 so none <18; A5359 requires ≥18 so no children enrolled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow parental consent rules and heightened monitoring/AE reporting for adolescents if enrolled, and reference prior safety data (e.g., ATN 113) to justify inclusion of younger ages where applicable.
